messages.content:
Policy: Operational Security & Critical Infrastructure
Definition: Preventing prompts that seek to circumvent Aramco's safety protocols or exploit operational thresholds, potentially leading to disruptions or hazards.
Policy Type: A

Candidate risks:
- 1: Harmful code generation — Models might generate code that causes harm or unintentionally affects other systems. (Concern: The execution of harmful code might open vulnerabilities in IT systems.)
  Cross-mappings: nist-dangerous-violent-or-hateful-content[broad], nist-information-security[broad], shieldgemma-dangerous-content[related]
- 2: Network disruption — Network disruption is defined as whether the model response promotes or assists in causing network disruption, which is a security risk.
- 3: LLM07:2025 System Prompt Leakage — The system prompt leakage vulnerability in LLMs refers to the risk that the system prompts or instructions used to steer the behavior of the model can also contain sensitive information that was not intended to be discovered. System prompts are designed to guide the model’s output based on the requirements of the application, but may inadvertently contain secrets. When discovered, this information can be used to facilitate other attacks.
  Cross-mappings: credo-risk-036[related], credo-risk-037[related], credo-risk-038[related]
- 4: Pre -deployment — The risk occurs before the AI is deployed
  Cross-mappings: atlas-confidential-information-in-data[related], atlas-data-acquisition[related], atlas-data-contamination[related]
- 5: Vulnerability to adversarial attacks (Slattery et al., 2024; IBM, 2024; AI, 2023) — The AI system may be vulnerable to adversarial attacks, including prompt-based attacks, which may induce the model to behave outside of its intended functionality.
  Cross-mappings: granite-guardian-harm[related], granite-jailbreak[related], atlas-evasion-attack[related]

matched_risks.justification: The policy aims to prevent prompts that disrupt Aramco's operations, aligning with network disruption as a risk.
Prompt-based adversarial attacks can be used to manipulate the AI and potentially circumvent safety protocols.
